Carbon stoichiometry normalized wrt C16:0 The concomitant oxidation of fadh2 is to account for the normalization to a saturated fatty acid (later in the mitochondria, the full beta oxidation cycle will occur, and the additional round of fad reduction will be balanced to account for the respective degree of desaturation). For example a 9,15 fatty acid would have 2fadh2(m) -> 2fad(m). The concomittant exchange for nadph is to account for cases in which the fatty acid has alternating odd and even double bonds (all human fatty acids?). For example a 9,12 fatty acid would have: fadh2(m) + nadph(m) + h(m) -> fad(m) + nadp(m). The nadph is from 2,4 dienoyl-CoA reductase (human gene: DECR1, gene ID 1666). PMID 7818482 (Koivuranta et al 1994) identified this as a mitochondrial gene, Voet and Voet claim this is peroxisomal (not directly supported with primary literature, so it is presumed to be mitochondrial). For all of the R-group reactions which lead to subsequent fatty acid oxidation, 3,2 enoyl-CoA isomerase activity (human gene: DCI, gene ID 1632) is "inherently" incorporated into the reactions. R1 - C16 groups R2 - essential FA + associated derivatives R3 - non-essential, dietary FA (C18) R4 - monounsaturated FA R5 -other (C26, C24) NJ

SAB This reaction represents the ATP driven secretion of dopa from the cell. It leaves out the vesicle because that is not a compartment. ATP:H ratio is assumed as 1:3 for vacuolar ATPase and substrate:h ratio is 1:2. This gives a 3:2 ratio for substrate:ATP

reaction.name: GABA secretion via secretory vesicle (ATP driven)

notes.html:p: Equation: (3) 4abut[c] + atp[c] + h2o[c] --> (3) 4abut[e] + adp[c] + h[c] + pi[c]

SAB This reaction represents the ATP driven secretion of glu from the cell. It leaves out the vesicle because a compartment is not available for that. ATP demand is not known for sure stoichiometrically, but 1:1 H coupling ratio is assumed, which could translate to 3 GABA/ATP.

Equation: [l] : (2) h2o + ksi_deg9 --> acgam + h + ksi_deg11 + so4

Note that this reaction is specific to beta-N-acetylhexosaminidase A and cannot be catalyzed by beta-N-acetylhexosaminidase B (or presumably beta-N-acetylhexosaminidase S). This is also a lumped reaction, representing the cleavage of GalNAc4S or GalNAc6S and N-acetylgalactosamine 4-sulfatase or 6-sulfatase. NCD
